verdict.rationale: Clerk can be driven without a browser through several of its own documented interfaces. It publishes a Backend API with an OpenAPI spec and personal access tokens for that API. It also offers API keys for programmatic callers explicitly including scripts and cron jobs, M2M tokens, and a CLI (`init`, `deploy`, `impersonate`, webhook relay) for scripted setup and deploys. Accountless agent registration and an MCP server with account tools for creating apps, managing users, and setting up production instances add further automation paths. missing for 10: explicit CI documentation (non-interactive CLI flags, env-var/token auth for CI runners, CI pipeline examples), independent or hands-on corroboration of headless/CI usage.
